body: Stop answer of a streamed session rides the stream as Op::Stream (merge=false) tracked in Live.waiting with its Held; a rewind holds unaccepted answers again (until >= retry+hold). Rejected: holding Op::Send in the scheduler broken gate (scheduler knows no barriers; a never-restarted topic would keep replies/prompts forever) and delaying hand-off until earlier lines are accepted (answer would land after next-turn lines already queued).

Rotation during a refusal: loss confirmed by a probe (Live of the ended session is dropped after its rewind, committed offset stays before the refused line); not fixed here, proposed as a separate task (drain an ended session stream before the next separator).

Verdict NEEDS_WORK rather than PASS: the re-held answer is paired to the next re-read TurnEnd by FIFO, so a rewind window that holds an earlier turn end whose answer was already accepted releases a later turn's answer before its own lines (probe confirms). Alternative considered: PASS with a follow-up task, rejected because this is the exact AC1 ordering the task fixes.

I1: pair answers with turn ends by transcript byte (Held.end set when paired; claim_end returns the claimed byte; accepted answer ends kept in Live.answered_ends until a barrier passes them, so a re-read end whose answer is in the topic lets nothing go; overdue re-held answers go first on the re-read). Rejected: keeping FIFO and only resetting ends_unclaimed after a rewind (still gives a later answer to an earlier re-read end).

I2: cap checked in answer_ops before any stream entry is created (room = MAX_QUEUED_MESSAGES - queued; no room -> Err -> send_text drops with the one overflow warn). Rejected: the review's drop in stream_answer, which would leave Waiting entries in Live forever (stream never stuck, never advances).

I3 documented, not fixed: holding a re-held answer past retry+hold until its re-read would need a second hard cap; chosen instead: a timed-out re-held answer records its turn end (answered_early) so the late re-read does not release another answer at it.

Verdict NO_SHIP rather than SHIP with a follow-up: an answer paired with a turn end but sent outside the stream (document >4 parts, over-cap drop, blank Stop) leaves no answered_ends mark, so a rewind re-read turns that end into an unclaimed end and the next Stop is released before its own lines (e2e reproduced 4/4). Alternative considered: SHIP since main was worse and the trigger is narrow; rejected because it breaks AC1 on a reproducible path and the fix is a few lines.

BUG-1: record the paired end of an answer that skips the stream unconditionally (deduplicated) in answer_ops, instead of QA's read_at < end variant, which is false on the claim and Release paths where the barrier already passed the end

Timeout release with end None left unfixed and documented: an owed-ends counter was rejected because several Stops per turn or a Stop without a turn end in the file would make every later answer wait its timeout

Round 2 verdict NO_SHIP rather than SHIP with a follow-up: BUG-1 is closed, but Live::turn_end consumes the answered_ends mark on the first re-read, so a second rewind to the same barrier forgets the end, the third read leaves it unclaimed and the next Stop goes out before its lines (two e2e tests via serve_agents, 3/3). Alternative considered: SHIP since nothing is lost; rejected because it breaks AC1 and a one-line fix (keep the mark, advance/rewind prune it) passes the whole cctg suite.

BUG-2: Live::turn_end keeps the answered_ends mark on re-read (only return None) instead of consuming it; alternative rejected: re-deriving the mark in rewind from a separate committed-answers list, which adds state that advance/rewind already bound by barrier offset.
